_about: Settings of RL2 for main_formulation_3. RL2 = the RL1 method (attention policy, imitation warm-up, REINFORCE with a shared baseline) with (a) changed training: bigger batches, more training on large n, a larger validation set, and (b) Efficient Active Search per test instance. Every value can also be overridden on the command line of train_rl2.py / solve_rl2.py. Formulation data (costs, fleet, T, ...) are NOT here: they come from dataset_ev_solomon/csv and code/f3_params.json.

generator._about: Random training instances (rl2_generator.py, same rules as RL1). Fleet, stations, costs, T, depot and city area come from the CSV dataset per (file size, class); these settings only shape the new random customers.

model._about: Policy network (rl2_model.Policy, same architecture as RL1): embedding size d, attention heads, encoder layers, feed-forward width, logit clipping C, hidden width of the small MLPs on the dynamic features.

training._about: As RL1, with three changes. batch_instances 64 (RL1: 32): a less noisy policy gradient. n_weight_power 1: a batch's n is drawn from [n_min, n_max] with probability proportional to n^n_weight_power (RL1: uniform), because the gap to the MILP was largest at n = 60-90. Validation on 4 sizes x 50 instances (RL1: 3 x 24), so the best epoch is chosen less by chance. Unchanged: first imitation_batches warm-up batches teach the greedy cost rule (teacher forcing); then REINFORCE, every instance rolled out `samples` times, baseline = mean cost of its own rollouts; training cost = Z + drop_penalty x (instance cost scale) per unplaced EV; lr (warm-up) and lr_reinforce (after it), decayed by lr_decay_per_epoch. Stop rules: the first min_epochs epochs always run; then stop after patience_epochs epochs without a better validation ratio (by more than min_improvement), at max_epochs in total, or after `hours`. Every run starts at epoch 1.

inference._about: solve_rl2.py, step 1 (run id rl2_sampling): per instance, `augment` symmetric copies of the map (rotations / reflections, 1..8) x (1 greedy rollout + `samples` sampled rollouts), as RL1; the plan with the fewest unplaced EVs, then the lowest Z, is kept. chunk = rollouts simulated together (memory).

active_search._about: solve_rl2.py, step 2 (run id rl2_eas): Efficient Active Search, EAS-Emb variant (Hottung, Kwon, Tierney, ICLR 2022). Starting from step 1's best plan, the trained network is frozen and only this instance's embeddings (the encoder output of each map symmetry) are updated for up to `iterations` iterations or `seconds` seconds, whichever comes first. Each iteration: `samples` sampled rollouts per symmetry; loss = REINFORCE with the shared baseline + `imitation_weight` x (negative log-likelihood of the best plan found so far, teacher forcing); Adam with learning rate `lr`. The best plan seen in any iteration is kept, so the result is never worse than step 1.
